### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/types/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**27** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fdb9a072a9a8ce50807ba0ce638264739a022158`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/types/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **23** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fdb9a072a9a8ce50807ba0ce638264739a022158` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2cda891e047c7fa12b7aee6708400bb313557224` — the merge of head `85872264d954a170e95b6787db3fbad904275c77` into base `fdb9a072a9a8ce50807ba0ce638264739a022158`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2cda891e047c7fa12b7aee6708400bb313557224 && git checkout 2cda891e047c7fa12b7aee6708400bb313557224
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fdb9a072a9a8ce50807ba0ce638264739a022158 85872264d954a170e95b6787db3fbad904275c77 && git checkout -B drift-repro fdb9a072a9a8ce50807ba0ce638264739a022158 && git merge --no-ff 85872264d954a170e95b6787db3fbad904275c77

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fdb9a072a9a8ce50807ba0ce638264739a022158
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fdb9a072a9a8ce50807ba0ce638264739a022158` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `38c6247211999216b682c58bfbeace9814d2f07a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/types/src/object-absence.ts, packages/types/src/object-absence.test.ts, packages/types/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/team-graph.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/position-graph.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/recipient-reads-complete.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/recipient-membership-recompute.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/position-graph.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/team-position-holders-complete.integration.test.ts + packages/types/src/keyset-walk.ts, packages/types/src/driver-error-classification.ts (matchesDriverError, MISSING_TABLE, namesAnotherRelation), packages/types/package.json, packages/core/src/utils/object-not-found.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (resolveObjectName), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/recipient-membership-recompute.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts (reconcileRuleForUser, ruleReachesUser, revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients, evaluateAllForRecord, evaluateAllRulesForObject), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/bu-tree-recompute.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/queue-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/index.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts (ITeamGraphService), packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts, docs/adr/0142-ownership-queue-membership-claim-and-assignment-rules.md (D2, D5, D6, D7), packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-team-member.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-position.object.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/filter-refusal.ts, .github/workflows/ci.yml (dogfood legs and dogfood-gate), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs (readClause2Line)

Inputs read: card #29503 body and all five comments (triage 6583253479, claim 6586753163, dev report 6588119628, claim amendment 6588159994, seat ruling 6588178193); PR #29602 body, 14-path file list, net diff `origin/main...pr29602` (merge-base `66ba23e4`); the 62 check-runs on the head, polled twice.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged against the tree:

1. **Sharing `TeamGraphService.expandUsers` (sys_team_member).** Now `readMembershipToCompletion` → `keysetWalk` pages of 10,000 ordered by `id`, projection `['id','user_id']`. Failed read: `holderReadRefusal` throws with the driver error as `cause`, before `cache.expandUsers.set`, so nothing is cached. Truncated walk (`walk.truncated`): throws the WALK_INCOMPLETE refusal. Absent object (`isObjectAbsentError(err,'sys_team_member')`): `null` → `[]`, cached as before. **Right.** The published contract (`ITeamGraphService.expandUsers`, sharing-service.ts L664) declares only "all user ids that are members of teamId"; it never declared an empty answer on failure, so no declared capability is taken away (see ④).
2. **`sys_user_position` limb of sharing `PositionGraphService.expandPositionUsers`.** Same walk, projection adds `valid_from`/`valid_until`; the ADR-0091 D2 `isGrantActive` filter is unchanged. A throw leaves `cache.expand` unset (the `set` is after both limbs); absence falls through to the `expandRoleUsers` transition limb, as before. **Right.** The `filter` → `where` key change is immaterial: ObjectQL treats `filter` as an alias slot of `where` (engine.ts RPC_QUERY_ALIAS_SLOTS), and the pre-existing #29362 walk already used `where` against the real engine.
3. **`teamHasMember` / `holdsRole`.** `probeMembership` keeps `limit: 1` (a one-row existence probe is never cut), absence → `[]` → `false`, every other failure throws a `'check'`-worded refusal. **Right.** **`holdsPosition`** became a 1,000-row walk (`pageRows: 1000`, `kind: 'check'`), refusing a failed assignment read instead of falling through to `holdsRole`; absence still falls through. **Right** — on main a user with more than 1,000 rows (lapsed history) whose only active row sat past the bound answered `false`, the same defect class as site 2.
4. **Who catches, and what the end caller sees** (read in the cited code, not the PR body):
   - Per-user recompute (`recipient-membership-recompute.ts` L305-L323): `reconcileRuleForUser` → `ruleReachesUser` → the probe rejects before the `revoke` loop; the per-(rule,user) catch warns `recipient membership re-evaluation failed`, grants stay. On main a `false` revoked every grant the user held from that rule (L1679-L1685). **Kept grant — right**, pinned in the 3 added recompute tests on the real engine.
   - Whole-rule passes: `evaluateAllForRecord` (per-rule catch L1424), `evaluateAllRulesForObject` (L1463), boot backfill and rebind in `sharing-plugin.ts` (L237, L510), `bu-tree-recompute.ts` (L290-L304) and `queue-hooks.ts` (L206-L235) around `revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients` / `evaluateRule` — every caller catches per rule and warns; the rule's existing grants stay. **Refused bulk pass, grants kept — right.**
   - Approvals `team` / `position` approver: `resolveApproverSpec`'s one try (L2566-L2603) sets `directoryFailure`, the slot falls back to its `type:value` literal and logs `could not be expanded — a directory or read-filter lookup failed` with `error`. **Skipped tier with a warning naming the failed read — right**, pinned in the two caller-sees tests.
   - Approvals `resolveAs` expressions (L2842-L2846): the existing catch swallows to `users = []` and pushes the `resolveAs:key` literal slot with **no warning** — the same posture #29497 accepted for a `sys_member` failure. Not a site of this card; noted for the seat below.
   - Approvals escalation (`escalateTo`, L7689-L7704): catch → literal → `reassignTargetRefusal` re-expands and the throw propagates out of the sweep; the next sweep retries (the body's account matches the code). Reassign door (`assertReassignTargetIsNotSubmitter`, `reassignTargetRefusal`): the throw reaches the caller as the request's error, as a `sys_member` failure already does since #29497 — a server-side failure, never a refusal naming the submitter.
5. **Approvals `expandTeamUsers`** through the new `readHoldersToCompletion` (one walk for tier, position and team; `HOLDER_PAGE_ROWS` 10000). `teamIsProvablyOutsideOrg` / `dropMembersProvablyOutsideOrg` are outside the walk and unchanged. **Right.**
6. **`isObjectAbsentError` attribution.** `isMissingTableError(error, readObject)` → `matchesDriverError`: at every node `relation = targetedTableOf(err) ?? readObject`, and MISSING_TABLE's `excludes.namesAnotherRelation(message, relation)` returns `false` for a missing-table phrase naming a different relation before any code/errno/message match. The `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` half compares `object === readObject` strictly; the engine's envelope (`objectNotFoundError`, core) always sets `object`. A real outage (SQLITE_IOERR, connection terminated, lock timeout, permission refusal) matches no MISSING_TABLE code, errno or phrase → `false` → refusal. Residual: a code-only PG `42P01` with no message would be attributed to `readObject`; both reads are plain-equality `where` with no relation path, so the only relation the statement touches is the object itself. **Right**; `object-absence.test.ts` pins another object's absence (both spellings), the unattributed code and three outages.
7. **`keysetWalk` termination and completeness.** No `max`, so `truncated` arises only from a row without `id` or a cursor that did not advance (judged by string equality on last/first, never JS order). The cursor strictly advances on every full page under a seeking driver, the set is finite, so the walk terminates; a non-seeking reader is reported truncated and refused, never spun. Completeness holds on `SqlDriver` (SQLite, PG, MySQL: ORDER BY and the `$gt` compare run under the same column collation) and on `driver-memory` (`$gt` is an executed operator). Both objects carry a text `id` (`sys-team-member.object.ts` L127, `sys-user-position.object.ts` L61). The 10,001-row tests on the real SQLite engine with scrambled ids count exactly 2 reads. **Right.**
8. **`holderCheck` in `ownership-queue-service.ts`.** Team: `teamHasMember` answered `false` on main (internal catch) and answers `false` now (wrapper catch + `warnOnce`), so the queue's team answer is byte-identical. Position: on main `holdsPosition` swallowed a failed `sys_user_position` read and fell through to `holdsRole`, and `expandPositionUsers` fell through to the `sys_member.role` limb — so on that outage a queue position spec contributed the transition-source holders; now `holderCheck` / `expandSpec` answer `false` / `[]`. That is exactly the header's declared posture ("a failed read of a member table contributes nobody for that specification"), reached for the first time — **right against the declaration**, but the PR body's row "Ownership queue … unchanged" and the changeset's "still contributes nobody" overstate it for the transition-limb case, and the `ownership-queue.test.ts` pin (fixture without `sys_member`) cannot see the difference. **Should-fix** (prose + pin), see ④.
9. **Public surface.** `@objectstack/types` gains `isObjectAbsentError` via `export * from './object-absence.js'` on the `.` entry (package.json exports → dist/index). `readMembershipToCompletion` and `probeMembership` are module exports of `team-graph.ts` but `plugin-sharing/src/index.ts` L49 exports only `TeamGraphService`, `expandPrincipal`, `TeamGraphOptions` — not public. No `@objectstack/core` export. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — the single line-initial declaration on both carriers (PR body L8, changeset L9); `readClause2Line` returns the first declaration and skips the body's L98 bullet (no colon-key, describing) and L99 (backticked inline key), so the level axis is measured. `Metadata-protocol: none` on both — right, no authorable key, value or type changes. Changeset `.changeset/29503-recipient-reads-complete.md`: `@objectstack/types: patch`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing: patch`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals: patch`. Right under AGENTS.md's rule ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner"): the new export is a non-protocol widening of types, and the refusals are a non-protocol narrowing of the two plugins. The types package takes a level, which the claim amendment required. The `!` title (`fix(plugins)!:`) and the **BREAKING** banner are present on both carriers; the ADR-0087 marker is one (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), correct since no author has anything to rewrite. The `yes` value is right: a new export is a widening in application code. Check Changeset and every Lint gate (which run `check-changeset-no-major`) concluded success on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Approvals `expandTeamUsers` fold-in** (not a numbered site, named by the card title): same table and defect as site 1, same file as site 2, same gate family, declared in the report and PR body. Within the in-place exemption. **Confirmed.**
- **`ownership-queue-service.ts` changed although the claim said "only if ADR-0142 allows":** the change is the forced consequence of sites 1-3 throwing — without `holderCheck`, `specsReachUser` would have started throwing into the access path and claim admission, a narrowing nobody ordered. ADR-0142 read: D2 says "An empty expansion is a fact, not a fault: the consumers below each say what they do with it"; D5 covers only an assignment-rule evaluation ("leaves the row as it was … logs at warn"); D6/D7 say what an empty slate/expansion does; the published `IOwnershipQueueService` header declares `null`/`[]`/`false` for a name that resolves nowhere and `[]` for an empty queue — nothing declares the failure posture. Only the service header does. The change keeps that header's posture. **Confirmed**; the ADR allows it because it does not speak.
- **`holdsPosition` 1,000-row read becoming a walk:** right (①.3); `pageRows` keeps the one-read case one read.
- **Forced fixture-id edits** in `ownership-queue.test.ts` and `position-graph.test.ts`: every row gains an `id`, no assertion changed (diff read whole); required because `keysetWalk` reports a row without its key as truncated and the read now refuses that. The same edit #29497 made for `sys_member`. **Confirmed.**
- **Dogfood reading vs the head's check-run.** The `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run concluded `success`, but its own log reads `leg dogfood (declared roster 1..3/3) — aggregate result: skipped` and `leg dogfood-verify — skipped`: by `ci.yml` design the three dogfood shards and `Dogfood Verify CLI` carry `github.event_name != 'pull_request'` in their `if:` and `dogfood-gate` counts zero expected attestations on a PR. So the head's dogfood check-run measures nothing; the only dogfood reading on this head is the dev's local battery (closure build 68/68, Test Files 397 passed / 3 skipped, Tests 3277 passed / 28 skipped, 0 failed), a dev reading, not a gate. The battery is measured on the push to `main`. Named here so the green is not read as a measurement.
- **Check-runs on the head at review time:** 62 runs. Completed success: Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate (legs skipped, above), Flag docs, Governed Surface Queue Guard, every Lint job (CI/release/engine gates, ESLint, PM dispatch-gates, docs & code guards, repo & tooling gates, three scoped), Live E2E UI, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Type Check consumer gates / debt ledger / source gates, filter, Auto Label. Skipped by design: 18.x harness, dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Lint UI, Packed-tarball smoke, Schedule gate, Temporal Conformance, UI Published Artifacts. **Still in progress:** Test Core (1/8 to 8/8), Test UI (1/16 to 16/16), Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace. The landing waits on those; this record's verdict is on the diff and the completed gates.
- **`open_questions[0]` (site 4):** seat ruled A on this PR, B as a follow-up card after an ADR-0142 amendment. **Confirmed.** B per consumer contradicts D2's one-expander sentence until amended, and `docs/adr/**` is Tier H, so folding it in would govern the whole PR. C is wrong as a direction: the access path and claim admission are correctly fail-closed. One addition for the B card: the position transition-limb case in ①.8 belongs to it (the queue's sharing-recipient pass through `isMember` now revokes on a `sys_user_position` outage where main kept the transition-source holders).
- **`open_questions[1]`:** seat settled A (`yes (narrowing)`). **Confirmed** (②).
- Out-of-scope findings (business-unit reads, `sys_queue_member` at QUEUE_READ_LIMIT, `organizationAdministrators` at APPROVER_INDEX_CAP) are correctly left unfiled by the dev and listed for the seat; the `resolveAs` silent swallow (①.4) is a fourth candidate of the same class.
- The three stray scratch files at the container root the report confesses are outside the tree and the PR; nothing in the diff carries them.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main`: `ITeamGraphService.expandUsers` and `expandRoleUsers` declare "all user ids that are members / hold the role" and nothing about failure; `IOwnershipQueueService` declares only the resolves-nowhere and empty-queue answers. No published contract ever declared "a failed read answers nobody", so this PR takes no declared capability away at a consumer — it makes a silent failure (an invented empty set that the reconcilers diffed into revocations, and a shrunk slate that looked complete) loud, which is exactly what the card asks. The one declared failure posture in the tree (the queue service header) is kept, through `holderCheck`, and the open question of whether it should change is routed to a ruling with the ADR amendment it needs. Pattern-wise the diff reduces copies: one walk per plugin, one absence predicate in types replacing two drifting `membershipObjectAbsent` copies, one refusal sentence family.

Attempts to break it, each read in the live tree:
- Infinite walk on a driver that ignores the seek: refused as truncated by the equality guard, never a hang (①.7).
- Absence of another object read as this one's, or an outage read as absence: excluded by `namesAnotherRelation` and the strict `object` compare; outages match no MISSING_TABLE signature (①.6).
- A cached failure: `cache.set` sits after the walk in both services; the not-cached test pins it on the real engine.
- A new 5xx at a request door: only the approvals reassign door and the escalation sweep propagate, and both already did so for `sys_member` since #29497; the sharing doors all catch per rule or per pair.
- A new refusal or a new "nobody" in the queue: team byte-identical; position moves from "transition-limb holders" to the header's declared "nobody" on a `sys_user_position` outage (①.8).

Findings:
- **Should-fix (prose + pin, not blocking):** the PR body's queue row and the changeset's "Ownership queues keep their declared posture … still contributes nobody" should say that on a `sys_user_position` outage a position specification now contributes nobody where it contributed the `sys_member.role` transition-source holders (the header's posture, newly reached); and the `ownership-queue.test.ts` posture pin should seed one `sys_member` transition row so the pin can see that answer. Either fold into the B follow-up card or amend the changeset body on this head.
- **Should-fix (follow-up, not this card):** approvals `resolveAs` expression catch (approval-service.ts L2842-L2846) swallows the refusal to a literal slot with no `could not be read` warning — pre-existing since #29497 for `sys_member`, now reached by team and position too. A class-a note for the seat's filing, same family.
- No must-fix.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · PR #29602 · 2026-11-02T21:37Z

Head-sha: `85872264d954a170e95b6787db3fbad904275c77`

**维护者速读(席位终稿)**
- **改了什么**:#29362 之后剩下的那批收件人读取，现在都读到完整为止，失败就报错。共享这边的 `sys_team_member`(团队成员)和 `sys_user_position`(岗位)按 id 翻页读完(每页 1 万行，用现成的 `keysetWalk`);`teamHasMember` / `holdsRole` / `holdsPosition` 读失败时报错，不再答「不是成员」。审批这边的团队和岗位收件人同样处理。对象本身不存在仍答「没有人」,判定函数 `isObjectAbsentError` 搬到 `@objectstack/types`,原来两份重复实现已删除。
- **为什么改**:#29503。之前按单个用户重算共享时，只要目录读失败一次，这个用户从该规则得到的授权就会全部被撤掉。现在授权保留，同时告警。
- **风险与回滚**:低到中。行为收窄(标题带 `!`):原来答空的失败路径现在报错。所有调用方都已按规则捕获，写入不会因此失败;审批槽位退回字面值并告警。所有权队列保持它已声明的「读失败即无人」,其中岗位规格在 `sys_user_position` 读失败时第一次真正走到这个答复(以前会退回 `sys_member.role` 的过渡持有人)。changeset 已写明。回滚即 revert。
- **先看**:`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/team-graph.ts`、`position-graph.ts`,`packages/types/src/object-absence.ts`。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing exec vitest run src/recipient-reads-complete.test.ts`,预期 16 条全绿(10,001 行 2 次读完)。
- **需要你做的**:无。席位按常设授权落地，合并即关 #29503。
- **席位意见**:可落。
